newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: STOCKS GAIN, BANKS TAKE BREATHER.
newsitem.headline: STOCKS GAIN, BANKS TAKE BREATHER.

text.p: Lithuanian usual market leaders Hermis and Vilniaus took a rest in Monday trading by the bourse close but brokers said they expected them again to wake up the sleepy stock exchange later this week.
Official list shares advanced 3.46 points to 944.30 points while the broader group A list inched up 2.94 points to 1832.13 points.
The gains came amid dismal central market turnover, which slid to 376,000 litas from an already low 457,000 litas.
"I would say that the market was not very strong," said one broker. "I think we'll have a pick up of turnover (this week)."
Hermis Bank, which led the central market with 1.6 million litas turnover last week, advanced to 215 litas from 212 but saw a mere 6,450 litas turnover.
Vilniaus Bank was steady at 243.20 litas in 24,000 litas central market turnover.
Brokers say that sellers in Hermis shares disappeared but with price at 215 litas, they may return soon. Dealers say Vilniaus Bank is also attractive at its current price.
"These (Vilniaus and Hermis) are the shares that are, lately, always interesting for investors," one broker said. "There should be some sellers.
Shares in Rokishkis Cheese, one of three corporates on the official list, were inactive on the central market, where they were unchanged from 42.00 litas.
Rokishkis found activity in block trades, though, where it turned over 203,000 litas at 40.50 litas.
Rokishkis on Monday announced its profits for the first six months of the year rose to 9.467 million litas from 1.25 million litas in the same period last year.
Brokers said the announcement came too late in the day for Rokishkis shares to be moved by the news.
"I think the price should react...maybe even tomorrow," said one broker.
